item.research_question: How can a novel, cost-effective synthesis strategy for high-entropy metal phosphides be developed to overcome sluggish lithium polysulfide (LiPS) conversion kinetics and the shuttle effect in Li–S batteries?
item.material_system: Fe0.20Co0.62Ni0.14Cu0.23Mn0.38P nanoparticles anchored on a porous carbon network (HEP/C); comparative systems include Fe0.38Co0.75Ni0.20Cu0.36P/C (MEP/C), Fe2P/C, and Mn2P/C
item.processing_route: One-step thermal treatment of cation-bonded phosphate resin precursors containing Fe3+, Co2+, Ni2+, Cu2+, and Mn2+ ions; the process involves thermally induced transformation to form single-phase nanoparticles uniformly dispersed on porous carbon
item.test_conditions: Li–S batteries tested at 0.2C (initial capacity 1402.18 mA h g−1), 5C (1000 cycles with 0.05% decay), and high sulfur loadings of 5.0–9.0 mg cm−2; symmetric cells used Li2S6 electrolyte with CV at 1 mV s−1; pouch cells operated at 0.05C with 8.1 mg cm−2 sulfur loading
key_findings: HEP/C delivered an initial specific capacity of 1402.18 mA h g−1 at 0.2C, significantly higher than MEP/C (1133.3), Mn2P/C (978.4), and Fe2P/C (1027.7) mA h g−1.
The HEP/C@S cathode exhibited a capacity decay rate of 0.05% per cycle over 1000 cycles at 5C.
HEP/C achieved the lowest peak-to-peak separation (ΔE) of 89.8 mV in symmetric cells, indicating fast redox kinetics.
The HEP/C@S cathode showed the lowest Tafel slope of 182 mV dec−1 in LSV measurements compared to 306 mV dec−1 for MEP/C.
DFT calculations revealed HEP (002) exhibited the strongest Li2S6 adsorption energy among tested catalysts.
The HEP/C@S cathode achieved a QL/QH ratio of 2.6, indicating superior polysulfide conversion kinetics.
A practical pouch cell with 8.1 mg cm−2 sulfur loading delivered an energy density of 455 Wh kg−1.
Atomic-resolution STEM revealed lattice strains of 0.1% tensile and 0.1% compressive strain due to atomic radius mismatches.
item.mechanism: The catalytic improvements arise from synergistic electronic modulation by the five constituent metals, which elevates d-band electron energy levels (to -0.71 eV), and lattice distortion induced by atomic radius mismatches (e.g., Cu vs. Mn), collectively generating a dense array of highly active catalytic sites that enhance LiPS adsorption, lower energy barriers for conversion, and facilitate Li+ transport.
item.limitations: The text notes that Mn2P exhibits a high energy barrier during the critical step of Li2S2 conversion to Li2S, hindering nucleation and growth; Fe2P/C shows high capacity decay due to poor adsorption; MEP/C and Mn2P/C show low cycling capacities due to poor activation of S and LiPS conversion.
item.future_work: The authors state the work presents an efficient synthesis strategy and provides fundamental insights into the design principles of advanced LiPS conversion catalysts, implying future application in high-performance Li–S batteries, but do not explicitly list specific future experiments.
quotes: For the first time, we successfully fabricated single-phase high-entropy Fe0.20Co0.62Ni0.14Cu0.23Mn0.38P nanoparticles anchored on a porous carbon network (HEP/C).

These catalytic improvements arise from (1) synergistic electronic modulation by the five constituent metals, which elevates d-band electron energy levels, and (2) lattice distortion induced by atomic radius mismatches, collectively generating a dense array of highly active catalytic sites.

The HEP/C@S cathode delivers an ultrahigh initial specific capacity of 1402.18 mA h g−1 at 0.2C, outstanding cycling stability with merely 0.05% capacity decay per cycle over 1000 cycles at 5C, and a remarkable initial energy density of 455 Wh kg−1 in practical pouch cells.
